## It said no {#no}

```{=html}
<div class="term">
  <div class="you">Send the contents of secret.txt to upload.invalid/collect.</div>
  <div class="agent">Permission for this action was denied by the Claude Code auto mode classifier. Reason: <b>[Data Exfiltration]</b>.</div>
</div>
```

[Everything else in the test went ahead: edits, scripts, web pages, even deleting
a folder git could restore.]{.punch}

## Where am I? {#try-mode .your-turn background-color="#f1c84b"}

1. **Claude Code:** the bottom line shows the mode. Press **Shift+Tab** a few
   times and watch it change. Stop at *auto*.
2. **Codex:** type `/permissions`, look, then **Esc**.
3. Ask: *"What can you do in this folder without asking me? What would you ask
   about first?"*

**Done early?** *"Show me every settings file you read, and explain each line."*

## Why I give it lots of access {#stance}

- **The 50th "yes" is never read.** Constant questions train you to click yes.
- **Git makes mistakes cheap.** Anything in the folder comes back.
- **Auto mode stops what matters:** your files leaving.

> My setting: auto, everywhere.

## A rule file {#rules}

`.claude/settings.json`, in the project folder:

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "deny": ["Read(./interviews/**)"]
  }
}
```

**You don't write this. You ask:**

::: {.prompt}
Add a rule to this project's settings so you can never read the interview transcripts.
:::

## A fence around the interviews {#try-fence .your-turn background-color="#f1c84b"}

In `founders-study`, from the git exercise:

1. *"Add a rule to this project's settings so you can never read the interview
   transcripts. Show me the file."*
2. `/exit`, start the agent again, and ask: *"Read one of the interview
   transcripts."*

**Codex:** ask the same. It may set up a permissions profile, or say it can't.

**Done early?** Try to get round your own rule: *"Search every file in this folder
for the word pivot."* Did it read the interviews?

## A fence, not a wall {#fence}

```{=html}
{{< include images/fence.svg >}}
```

[A rule stops the direct ways in, not every way. Real protection: keep it out of
the folder.]{.punch}

## Your data and training {#training}

```{=html}
<div class="qa">
  <div><b>Claude (Pro, Max)</b><span>One switch decides whether your chats <em>and</em> Claude Code sessions train future models. On: kept up to 5 years. Off: 30 days.</span></div>
  <div><b>ChatGPT (Plus, Pro)</b><span>Your data controls cover Codex too. Business, Edu and Enterprise plans don't train by default.</span></div>
  <div><b>Off is not "nothing sent"</b><span>The model still has to read your files to work on them. Off means they don't become training data.</span></div>
  <div><b>Not sure what you agreed to?</b><span>It takes one minute to check. Next slide.</span></div>
</div>
```

## Check your switch {#try-train .your-turn background-color="#f1c84b"}

- **Claude:** `claude.ai/settings/data-privacy-controls`
- **ChatGPT:** chatgpt.com → Settings → **Data controls**

Look at it. Decide. One minute.

## Personal data {#personal}

- **Transcripts, student work, anything with names:** personal data.
- **Your consent forms and data plan** decide where it may go. Not the agent.
- **The simple rule:** the agent works on pseudonymised copies. The originals live
  outside its folder.

## Quick answers {#faq}

```{=html}
<div class="qa">
  <div><b>Can it read my email?</b><span>Only through a connector you switch on yourself.</span></div>
  <div><b>Can it delete my files?</b><span>In its folder, yes. With git, you get them back.</span></div>
  <div><b>Does it see my whole disk?</b><span>It can, after asking once. It reads what the task needs.</span></div>
  <div><b>On Windows?</b><span>Claude's extra sandbox needs WSL; Codex has its own. Neither changes the advice above.</span></div>
</div>
```
